nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِي شِيَعِ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
That is, the sects of the ancients.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَِ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ḥumayd, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: Thus We insert the shirk. [Translator's note: so printed («الحسين»); al-Ḥasan (al-Baṣrī) is probably meant.]
Abū ʿUbayd said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us from Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»], from Mujāhid, who said: We insert the giving of the lie.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view held by the exegetes and the people of language, except those who deviate among them; for some of them said: the meaning is "thus We insert the Qurʾān." They argued that when the Prophet ﷺ recited the Qurʾān to them and made them hear it and it reached their hearts — and that was by Allah's command and power — it was Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, who inserted it into their hearts in this sense.
And it was said: since He created them with a constitution by which they understand the revelation that comes to them — when He created them with a constitution by which they understand what inserts that into their hearts, it is as though He inserted it.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتْ سُنَّةُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
That is, their way has gone before in giving the lie to the signs and proofs, and in their unbelief; and these are following in their footsteps.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِم بَاباً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ فَظَلُّواْ فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, and the angels kept ascending through it,
i.e. going and coming.
The people of language said: عَرَجَ يَعْرُجُ when he ascends and rises; and from it is the common people's saying: "So-and-so's soul was taken up (ʿurija)."

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿لَقَالُواْ إِنَّمَا سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصَارُنَا﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: (Our eyes) have been seized.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known of the reading of Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan is (سُكِرَتْ) without shadda.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, bewitched.
Abū ʿUbayd related from Abū ʿUbayda that one says سُكِرتْ أبصارهم when a dimness (samādīr) covers them so that they do not see.
Al-Farrāʾ said: Whoever read (سَكِرِتْ) took it from the stillness of the wind. [Translator's note: the vowelling «سَكِرِتْ» is as printed.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another, and their root is what Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is from intoxication (al-sukr) from drink.
This is a good view: i.e. something covered them that veiled their sight, as something covers the drunkard that veils his mind.
And sukūr of the wind is its stillness and abating, and that goes back to the meaning of al-takhyīr. [Translator's note: so printed («التخيير»); perhaps «التحيير», "bewilderment," is meant.]

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاءِ بُرُوجاً وَزَيَّنَّاهَا لِلنَّاظِرِينََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Meaning the stars.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And whoever said that they are the twelve zodiacal signs (burūj), his view goes back to this, because they are great stars.
It is well known in the language that one says بَرَج يَبْرُجُ when something appears and rises; so these stars were called burūj because of their visibility, their fixedness and their height. And al-barajj is largeness of the eye.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَّجِيمٍٍ﴾.
That is, he does not reach it, nor hear anything of the revelation except by stealth. This was one of the signs of the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ: we know of no poet who compared anything to the speed of the (shooting) stars except in Islam; had this existed before it, they would have used it as a comparison. [Translator's note: the source has «قله», evidently for «قبله», "before it".]
Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] said: al-rajīm is the accursed.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Every rajīm in the Qurʾān means "the reviled."
And it was said: rajīm means marjūm ("stoned"), i.e. he is pelted with the stars.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍٍ﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ﴾.
He said: That is, known.
Likewise ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated it from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
Abū Ṣāliḥ and ʿIkrima said: That is, measured out.
Mujāhid said: That is, determined by a measure.
Its meaning is: determined, not exceeding Allah's measure nor falling short of it, so it is as though it were weighed.
And it was said: by mawzūn He means what is weighed, of gold, silver, iron, lead and the like.
On this basis the meaning is: and We caused to grow in the mountains of every weighed thing.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوْ كَانُواْ مُسْلِمِينَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "A group of the monotheists will enter the Fire, and the polytheists will say to them: What use was your Islam and your faith to you, when you are with us in the Fire? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will bring them out of it, and at that point ﴿يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَروُا لَوْ كَانُوا مُسْلِمِين﴾."
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: That is on the Day of Resurrection.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: (The polytheists will say to those of the monotheists who were made to enter the Fire: What you were upon has not benefited you, and you are in the Fire! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will be angered on their behalf, and they will be brought out to a river called "the River of Life," and they will grow (anew) in it. Then a mark will remain on their faces by which they are known; it will be said: These are "the Jahannamīs." They will ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, to remove that from them, and He will remove it from them and admit them to Paradise. Then the polytheists will wish that they had been Muslims.)
And it was said: When the polytheists see (the truth) with their own eyes, they will wish for Islam.
As for the meaning of (رُبَّ) here: in the speech of the Arabs it is for diminution (taqlīl), and it carries a sense of threat. The Arabs use this a great deal for one whom they threaten and menace [Translator's note: the source has «تتخدّده», evidently for «تتهدّده», "menace"]. A man says to another: "Perhaps you will regret what you are doing" [and they are doubtful of his regretting and do not intend to make it little]; rather, the real meaning is that he is saying: even if it were something that happens rarely, or only once, you ought not to do it.
As for the statement of whoever said that «رُبَّ» is used for multiplicity (taktīr), it is not known in the speech of the Arabs.
And it was said: This will only be on the Day of Resurrection, when they recover from the terrors they are in, so it will be only in some of the stations.
The first view is the soundest.
The proof that it is a warning and a threat is His saying after it: ﴿ذَرْهُمْ يَأْكُلُوا وَيَتَمَتَّعُوا وَيُلْهِهِمُ الأَمَلُ، فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُون﴾.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشََ﴾.
That is, in the earth.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَن لَّسْتُمْ لَهُ بِرَازِقِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Meaning the beasts and the livestock.
Others said: Meaning the slaves and the beasts.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is more fitting, because (مَنْ) is not used for what lacks reason unless beings with reason are mixed in with it.
The meaning is: and We made for you the slaves, the beasts and the livestock.
And it is possible that the meaning is: We gave you a livelihood, and gave a livelihood to those for whom you are not providers.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ عِندَنَا خَزَائِنُهُ﴾.
He informed that the treasuries of things are in His hand,
i.e. that He, Mighty and Majestic is He, is their keeper and the One in charge of managing them.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا ٱلرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The wind carries the water and fertilises the clouds and milks them, so they flow as the milch-camel (al-laqḥa) gives milk; then it rains.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The winds fertilise the trees and the clouds, and milk them.
Abū Rajāʾ said: I said to al-Ḥasan: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا ٱلرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ﴾. He said: They fertilise the trees. I said: And the clouds? He said: And the clouds.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿لَوَاقِح﴾ means malāqiḥ; he holds that it is the plural of mulqiḥa and mulqiḥ, with the augment letters then dropped from it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is far-fetched; dropping augment letters from the like of this is permissible only in poetry. Rather, it is the plural of lāqiḥa.
And «لاَقِحٌ» is literal, without any omission, and it has one of two senses: it may be called lāqiḥ by way of attribution (ʿalā l-nasab), i.e. possessing fertilisation, as though it fertilises the clouds and the trees, as came in the exegesis — and this is the view of Abū ʿAmr.
And it may be called lāqiḥ meaning "pregnant/bearing." The Arabs call the south wind lāqiḥ and ḥāmil ("bearing"), and the north wind ḥāʾil ("barren") and ʿaqīm ("sterile"). And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿حَتَّى إذَا أَقَلَّتْ سَحَابَاً ثِقَالاً﴾ — and «أقلَّت» and «حَمَلَت» ("carried") are one.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿المستقدِمُونَ﴾ are the first generations, and ﴿المستأخِروُن﴾ are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ.
And Sufyān narrated from his father, from ʿIkrima, who said: ﴿المستقْدِمون﴾ are all who have come forth (into existence), and ﴿المستأخِروُن﴾ are all who were in the loins of men.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: ﴿المستقدِمُون﴾ are those who have died, and ﴿المستأخِروُنَ﴾ are the living.
And Sufyān narrated from Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, from Abū l-Jawzāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ﴾ — the first row; ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾ — the last row.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying: Nūḥ ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Mālik narrated to us from Abū l-Jawzāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾ — he said: A beautiful woman used to pray with the Prophet ﷺ. Some men would move forward so as not to see her, and some men would move back, and when the Prophet ﷺ bowed, one of them would put his hand on his knee and look at her from under his upper arm. So Allah sent down ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ مِن صَلْصَالٍٍ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them was narrated by Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-ṣalṣāl is dry clay.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: It is clay that dries and comes to have a clinking sound (ṣalṣala).
The other view was narrated by Ibn Abī Najīḥ and Ibn Jurayj from Mujāhid, who said: al-ṣalṣāl is the stinking. [Translator's note: the source has «ابن نجيح» and «ابن جريح».]
Abū Jaʿfar said: Both views are possible, though the first is clearer, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالفَخَّارِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda related that dry clay is called ṣalṣāl so long as fire has not touched it; once fire has touched it, it is fakhkhār (pottery).
The people of language recited:
* "كَعَدْوِ المُصَلْصِلِ الجَوَّالِ" *
(Like the running of the roaming, clattering one.)
And al-ṣalṣala is sound.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is pure clay mixed with sand, so a clinking is heard from it.
As for the second view: its origin is ṣilāl, then one of the two lāms was replaced by a ṣād.
[And al-Kisāʾī related that one says صلَّ اللحمُ and أصلَّ when meat goes rotten.]
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ﴾.
[al-ḥamaʾ and al-ḥamaʾa are] black, altered [clay].
There are four views on al-masnūn:
Sufyān narrated from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-masnūn is the stinking.
Likewise Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Man was created from ṣalṣāl, from sticky clay (ṭīn lāzib), which is the good, and from ḥamaʾ masnūn, which is the stinking.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: It is the stinking.
Of the people of language, al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī held this view. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī claimed that the saying of Allah ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾ is from this, and that its origin is (لَمْ يَتَسَنَّنْ), with one of the two nūns replaced by a hāʾ. So this is one view.
The other view — the position of Abū ʿUbayda — is that al-masnūn is "the poured."
And Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-masnūn is the moist.
This is in the sense of "the poured," because it can only be poured when it is moist. This is a good view, because one says سَننْتُ الشَّيءَ, i.e. "I poured it," and in the ḥadīth: "al-Ḥasan used to pour (yasunnu) water over his face"; and if this were from أَسِنَ الماءُ ("the water became stagnant"), it would be muʾsin.
The third view is that of al-Farrāʾ: it is "the rubbed/smoothed," and it can only be altered, from سننْتُ الحديدَ ("I whetted the iron").
The fourth view: it is what is poured into a mould and a form, from sunnat al-wajh (the contour of the face).

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ﴾.
That is, a term which it neither precedes nor goes beyond.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا بِٱلْمَلائِكَةِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾.
The meaning of (لَوْ مَا), (لَوْلاَ) and (هَلاَّ) — "why not?" — is one. The people of language recited:
تعدُّونَ عَقْر النِّيبِ أفضلَ مجدِكُمْ * بَنِي ضَوْطَرَى لَوْلاَ الكَمِيَّ المُقَنَّعَا
(You count the hamstringing of old she-camels as your finest glory, O sons of Ḍawṭarā — why not the helmeted, fully armed warrior?)
i.e. why do you not count the helmeted, fully armed warrior?
And Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»], who said: In this there is fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr).
He holds that its answer is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَوْ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ بَابَاً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَظَلُّوا فِيهِ يَعْرُجُون﴾; he holds that this is connected with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿لَّوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا بِٱلْمَلائِكَةِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿مَا نُنَزِّلُ ٱلْمَلائِكَةَ إِلاَّ بِٱلحَقِّ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, with the message and the punishment.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ إِذاً مُّنظَرِينَ﴾.
That is, if the angels came down, they would not be given respite, nor would their repentance be accepted, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنَا مَلَكَاً لَقُضِيَ الأَمْرُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ﴾.
Thābit and Qatāda said: Allah has guarded it from the devils adding falsehood to it or removing truth from it.
Mujāhid said: It is with Us.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ، إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْمَعْلُومِ﴾.
Sufyān said: It has reached me that the known time is the first blowing (of the Trumpet).

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ [verse 41].
One of the two (views) — and it is the position of Mujāhid — he said: The truth: its path is upon Me, and it comes back to Me; as is said by way of threat: "Your path is upon me (i.e. leads past me), so do what you will," and as the Exalted said: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ﴾. [Translator's note: the source begins «أحدهما» ("one of the two") without first announcing two views.]
The other view: This is a path according to My command and under My will.
And Qays ibn ʿUbāda read ﴿قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ and said: i.e. lofty; its meaning is lofty in religion and truth. [Translator's note: the reading is printed identically to the muṣḥaf; the gloss "lofty" implies the reading «عَلِيٌّ».]

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَاوِينَ﴾ [verse 42].
That is, the astray.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمَوْعِدُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ، لَهَا سَبْعَةُ أَبْوَابٍ لِكُلِّ بَابٍ مِّنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَّقْسُومٌ ٌ﴾.
That is, each of them has a station in the torment according to the degree of his station in sin.
And Mālik ibn Mighwal narrated from Ḥumayd, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hell has seven gates; one gate of them is for whoever draws his sword against my community" — or he said: "against the community of Muḥammad."

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَاناً عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ﴾.
Al-ghill according to the people of language is rancour, resentment and enmity; from it one says غَلَّ يَغِلُّ.
And from al-ghulūl — which is stealing from the spoils — one says غَلَّ يَغُلُّ; and from treachery one says أَغَلَّ يُغِلُّ, as the poet said: [Translator's note: the source has «ويُغال», evidently for «ويُقال», "one says".]
جَزَى اللَّهُ عَنَّا جَمْرَة ابنةَ نَوْفَلٍ * جَزَاءَ مُغِلٍّ بالأَمانةِ كَاذِب
(May Allah repay Jamra daughter of Nawfal on our behalf with the repayment of one treacherous with a trust, a liar.)
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِخْوَاناً عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿مُتَقَابِلِينَ﴾ — he said: None of them looks at the back of his companion's head.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيهَا نَصَبٌٌ﴾.
That is, fatigue.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَبِّىءْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾.
That is, inform.
And it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ came out to his Companions while they were laughing, and said: Do you laugh while Paradise and the Fire are before you? That weighed heavily on them, so Allah sent down ﴿نَبِّىءْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ لاَ تَوْجَلْ﴾.
Its meaning is: do not be alarmed. And al-qāniṭūn are the despairing.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱمْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْنَآ إِنَّهَا لَمِنَ ٱلْغَابِرِينَ﴾.
It was said: «قَدَرْنَا» means "We knew"; and «قدَّرنا» is in its proper sense, i.e. it is in Our decree and in what We informed him of, thus.
Al-ghābir is the one who remains, and it may be used for the one who departs. The meaning is: she is among those who remain behind in the destruction. The people of language recited:
لا تَكْسَعِ الشَّوْلَ بِأَغْبَارِهَا * إنَّكَ لا تَدْرِي مَنَ النَّاتِجُ
(Do not leave the dry she-camels with the remnants of their milk unmilked; you do not know who will deliver their young.)
Al-aghbār are the remnants of milk.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Lūṭ ﷺ did not recognise them.
And it was said: Ibrāhīm ﷺ found them strange, because they did not eat of his food; and they used to regard a guest as suspect if he did not eat.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ بَلْ جِئْنَاكَ بِمَا كَانُواْ فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: With the punishment.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: rather, we have come to you with what they used to doubt — the descent of the punishment upon them.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾.
Al-surā (night travel) is only by night; but His saying, the Exalted, ﴿بِقِطَعٍ﴾ indicates that much of the night has passed.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ﴾.
It was said: He forbade turning to look at what was in the dwellings, lest they be distracted by it from going on.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ ٱلأَمْرَ﴾.
That is, We informed him of it; then He explained it, saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَنَّ دَابِرَ هَؤُلآءِ مَقْطُوعٌ مُّصْبِحِينَ﴾.
That is, the last of them would be uprooted.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-dābir is the root.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قَالُواْ أَوَلَمْ نَنْهَكَ عَنِ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
It is narrated that they had forbidden him to host anyone as a guest.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ هَؤُلآءِ بَنَاتِي إِن كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ﴾.
This answer is construed according to the sense. The meaning is: they wanted them (the guests) for depravity, so Lūṭ ﷺ said to them: These are my daughters, so marry.
The best of what has been said on this is that the wives of every prophet are in the position of mothers of his community, and the children of his community are in the position of his children.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونََ﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿لَعَمْرُكَ﴾ — by your life (laʿayshuka).
And Abū l-Jawzāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: By your life (laḥayātuka).
And it is narrated that Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī disliked that a man should say laʿamrī; he said: because its meaning is "by my life."
And so it is according to the people of language.
Sībawayh said: al-ʿamr and al-ʿumr are one, and in oaths they use only the fatḥa, because of its lightness; and laʿumurī has been related; all of it means al-ʿumr (life).
This is a distinction for the Prophet ﷺ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, swore by his life.
Abū l-Jawzāʾ said: I have not heard of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, swearing by the life of anyone other than him ﷺ.
Sufyān said: I asked al-Aʿmash about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾.
He said: He swore by the Prophet that they are wandering to and fro in their heedlessness.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ مُشْرِقِينََ﴾.
That is, the Cry seized them with the punishment at the time of sunrise.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِلْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, for those who discern by signs (al-mutafarrisīn).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, for those who look.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its real sense is: توسَّمتُ الشيءَ — I looked at the thing with the look of one who verifies, until the reality of the thing's mark (sima) became established.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّهَا لَبِسَبِيلٍ مُّقِيمٍ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is "and the signs (are…)," and it is possible that the meaning is "and the city of the people of Lūṭ (is…)."
Mujāhid said: ﴿لَبِسَبِيلٍ مُّقِيمٍ﴾ — on a marked road, i.e. a clear one.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأَيْكَةِ لَظَالِمِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-ayka is the thicket full of trees.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so it is in the language: a tree is called ayka, and its plural is ayk.
And it is narrated that their trees were dawm (doum palms).
As for the narration of whoever narrated that «لَيْكَةَ» is the name of the town in which they were, and (الأيكةُ) is the whole country, it is not known in the language and is not sound.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمَا لَبِإِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, on a clear road, i.e. they pass by them on their journeys.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the language that a road is called imām, because it is followed and taken as a guide.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلحِجْرِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: al-Ḥijr is the valley; he holds that it is its name.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانُواْ يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتاً آمِنِينَ﴾.
That is, secure (in the belief) that they would not fall down.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱصْفَحِ ٱلصَّفْحَ ٱلْجَمِيلََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: This was before he was commanded to fight.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾.
ʿAbd Khayr narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he said regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾: meaning the Opening of the Book (al-Fātiḥa).
Likewise Abū Hurayra said: It is the Opening of the Book, and «In the name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful» is not part of it.
Likewise Abū Yaḥyā narrated from Mujāhid, and likewise Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda.
And Sufyān ibn Manṣūr narrated from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾. [Translator's note: so printed («سفيان بن منصور»); probably "Sufyān, from Manṣūr".]
He said: The seven long ones (al-sabʿ al-ṭuwal).
Likewise Shuʿba narrated from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾.
He said: The seven long ones: "al-Baqara, Āl ʿImrān, al-Nisāʾ, al-Māʾida, al-Anʿām, al-Aʿrāf and Yūnus."
So it is in the ḥadīth; and likewise al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the seven long ones. And likewise Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: "The seven oft-repeated (al-sabʿ al-mathānī) and the Mighty Qurʾān: the Mother of the Qurʾān."
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿ٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ﴾ — the rest of it.
And it is authentically reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he said: The seven mathānī are al-Ḥamd (al-Fātiḥa); and Qatāda held this.
He explained its meaning, saying: because the Opening of the Book is repeated (tuthannā) in every rakʿa, obligatory or supererogatory.
The meaning on this view is: and We have given you seven verses of what is repeated in the prayer.
And (مِنْ) here, on this view, is for explaining the genus (li-bayān al-jins), as the Exalted said: ﴿فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْس مِنَ الأوْثَانِ﴾.
And it is possible that the meaning is: of that by which Allah is praised (yuthnā), because in al-Ḥamd there is praise (thanāʾ) of Allah, mention of His oneness and of His sovereignty over the Day of Judgement; and on this view (مِنْ) is also for explaining the genus.
And it is possible that it is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), the meaning being: and We have given you seven verses of the mathānī, i.e. of the Qurʾān, in which the verses and stories are repeated and in which Allah is praised.
This is better, and it is the position of Abū Mālik, because he said: ﴿المثاني﴾ is the Qurʾān.
As for those who said they are the seven long ones, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explained his position, saying: because the legal limits and the obligations are repeated in them; so (من) on this view is for explaining the genus.
And it is possible that it is partitive, as preceded.
And Abū ʿUbayd narrated that Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna used to recite this verse, interpreting it in light of the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "He is not of us who does not yataghanna with the Qurʾān" — he said: i.e. make himself free of need through it (yastaghnī).
He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded the Prophet ﷺ to be free of need of wealth through the Qurʾān, and the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي وَٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّنْهُمْ﴾.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that he said: "Whoever has memorised the Qurʾān and then considers that anyone has been given something better than what he was given has belittled something great [and magnified something small]."
Mujāhid said regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لاَ تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّنْهُمْ﴾:
He said: The rich, the ones alike, i.e. likes of one another in blessings.
And al-azwāj in the language are the kinds.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلْ إِنِّيۤ أَنَا ٱلنَّذِيرُ ٱلْمُبِينُ. كَمَآ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى ٱلْمُقْتَسِمِينَ﴾.
There is an omission in the statement, and the meaning is: and say, I am the clear warner (of) a punishment like that which We sent down upon al-muqtasimīn.
There are several views about al-muqtasimīn:
One of them: they were a group who swore an alliance to slander (ʿaḍh) the Prophet ﷺ.
The other view: al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿كَمَآ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى ٱلْمُقْتَسِمِينَ﴾, that he said: the Jews and the Christians; ﴿الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا القُرْآنَ عِضِين﴾ — he said: they believed in part of it and disbelieved in part of it.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿المقتسمين﴾ are the People of the Book; they tore the scriptures apart and rejoiced in what they had of them.
Mujāhid said: ﴿المقتسمين﴾ are the people of the (various) religions.
Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] said, and ʿAṭāʾ said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh; they tore apart what they said about the Qurʾān: some of them said it is poetry, some said it is sorcery, and some said it is tales of the ancients; and that is the ʿiḍūn.
ʿIkrima said: ﴿عِضِين﴾ is sorcery.
Abū ʿUbayda held that ﴿عِضِينَ﴾ is taken from al-aʿḍāʾ (limbs).
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is a good view, i.e. they divided up what they said. And he recited:
* "وَلَيْسَ دِينُ اللَّهِ بالمُعَضَّى" *
(And the religion of Allah is not one to be cut into pieces.)
i.e. not divided.
Al-Farrāʾ held that it is taken from al-ʿiḍāh, which are (thorny) trees.
And al-Kisāʾī held that it may be taken from both.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, recite the Qurʾān aloud in the prayer.
He said: And from it: تَصَدَّع القومُ, when the people disperse.
He said: And from it al-ṣudāʿ (headache), because it is a splitting of the sutures of the head.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known among the people of language that one says صَدَع بالحق when he makes it clear and manifest; it is as if (it says): make clear and make manifest.
Abū ʿUbayda recited (the verse) of Abū Dhuʾayb describing a herd of wild asses and jennies, and that he (the stallion) rules over them:
وكَأَنَّهُنَّ رِبابةٌ وكأَنَّه * يَسَرٌ يُفِيضُ على القِدَاحِ ويَصْدَعُ
(As if they were a bundle of gaming arrows, and he a gambler who shuffles the arrows and declares (the winning one).)
And from this the dawn is called ṣadīʿ, as he said:
* "كأنَّ بَيَاضَ لَبَّتِه صَدِيعُ" *
(As if the whiteness of its breast were the breaking dawn.)
And Abū l-ʿAbbās (al-Mubarrad) held that the meaning is: split falsehood with what you are commanded, i.e. separate (it).

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاكَ ٱلْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ﴾.
"Abū Bakr" Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda — and ʿUthmān al-Jazarī from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās — regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاكَ ٱلْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ﴾. [Translator's note: so printed; the chain is presumably "Salama ibn Shabīb, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq".] They both said: "The mockers" were al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, ʿAdī ibn Qays, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth and al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib. They passed one by one by the Prophet ﷺ while Jibrīl, peace be upon him, was with him; and whenever one of them passed, Jibrīl said to him: How do you find this one? He would say: An evil servant of Allah. And Jibrīl would say: We have sufficed you against him.
As for al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, he stumbled, and an arrow caught in his cloak; he went to sit down and it cut his median vein (akḥal), and he bled until he died.
As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, a branch with thorns was brought, and his face was struck with it, so that his eyeballs ran down over his face. He used to say: I made a prayer against Muḥammad and he made a prayer against me, and mine was answered and his was answered. He prayed against me that I be blind, and I became blind; and I prayed against him that he be alone and outcast among the people of Yathrib, and so he was.
As for al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, he trod on a thorn, and his flesh fell away from his bones until he perished.
As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib and ʿAdī ibn Qays, one of them got up in the night, at ease, to drink from a jar, and he kept drinking until his belly burst and he died; and as for the other, a snake bit him and he died.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُنْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّاجِدِينََ﴾.
That is, be among those who pray.

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: Except three verses, which were revealed between Mecca and Medina when the Prophet ﷺ returned from Uḥud — Ḥamza having been killed and mutilated. The Prophet said: "I will surely mutilate thirty of them," and the Muslims said: "We will surely mutilate them." So Allah sent down ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُم فعَاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقبْتُم بِهِ﴾ to the end of three verses.
[Translator's note: this passage is filed under 15:99 but evidently belongs to the introduction of Sūrat al-Naḥl (16), whose Meccan revelation is being stated, with the exception of three verses (16:126–128).]
